experimental_design: All seeds were placed on water agar plates at 100% concentration with no additional additives. Seeds with positioned with sterilized tweezers, with four seeds in each treatment group so sample size/repetitions = 4. Each plate was tested with a different substance, but the left half of the plates were additionally tested with 5 µL of nystatin to test for growth inhibition with nystatin additive under all conditions. Therefore, each plate contained two treatment groups with four seeds each, so each plate contained eight radish seeds. All treatments were applied directly to seeds by pipette. Plates were assigned letter IDs to make the explanation of the experimental design easier; photos of the plates are attached under "additional notes". Plate A was inoculated with 5 µL of water; plate B was inoculated with 5 µL of ethyl acetate; plate C was inoculated with 2.5 µL of JB5 chemical extract; plate D was inoculated with 5 µL of JB5 chemical extract. JB5 extract was resuspended in 80 µL of ethyl acetate prior to the application of the extract to the seeds. Water (A) and ethyl acetate (B) plates were used as controls to ensure that the seeds would germinate under optimal conditions (with only water added) and to ensure that the ethyl acetate used to resuspend the JB5 chemical extract would not interfere with the germination of the radish seeds. Plates treated with the JB5 chemical extract (C and D) were the experimental groups.

experimental_design: Before performing the experiment, I performed a chemical extraction and resuspended my extract in ethyl acetate. I used a total of 4 water agar plates and 16 radish seeds. I placed 4 radish seeds on each water agar plate. I labeled each plate. On plate one, I covered each radish seeds with 10 microliters of water using a micropipet and distilled water. On plate two, I covered each radish seed with 10 microliters of ethyl acetate using a micropipet. One plate three, I covered each radish seed with 10 microliters of my extract using a micropipet. On plate four, I covered each radish seed with 5 microliters of my extract and 5 microliters of ethyl acetate using a micropipet. I then incubated all four plates at room temperature for 7 days (168 hours) and examined the results.
results:
The growth of the radish seeds was not inhibited on plates one, two, three, or four. The radish seeds were able to grow substantially. The amount of growth of the radish seeds was extremely similar on all four plates. On plate one, all four radish seeds grew more than two inches. On plate two, all four radish seeds grew more than two inches. On plate three, all four radish seeds grew more than two inches. On plate four, all four radish seeds grew more than two inches. 
 My results showed that my extract was not toxic to radish seeds, indicating that it is not toxic to eukaryotic cells and may be beneficial in future clinical use.

experimental_design:
Test condition: chemical extract from isolate AG9 
 Control conditions: water and ethyl acetate 
  
 To begin this experiment, we made a chemical extract with our isolate AG9 and resuspended it in ethyl acetate. This became our test condition. For each seed, we used a micro pipet to pipet 10 microliters of our chemical extract to one radish seed. This process was repeated 4 times and with each of the control conditions as well (4 water agar plates, with 3 seeds each). We then left the radish seeds to grow for 48 hours. After 48 hours we examined out plates to see if there had been any growth. We then left the seeds to grow for an additional 120 hours until we checked again for more growth.
results: After 48 hours, there was growth in all of the seeds that were treated under control conditions (8 seeds, 4 for each condition). This means that neither of the control conditions would inhibit the growth of eukaryotic organisms. In addition, there was little to no growth of the seeds that were treated with our chemical extract, however, we could see that some of the seeds were beginning to crack (1 seed had little growth, 3 seeds beginning to crack). After an additional 120 hours, we saw growth from all but one of the seeds (11 seeds total, test and control conditions) and the amount of growth was consistent across each of the conditions. The one seed that did not show growth was treated with our chemical extract, however, it was also beginning to show signs of growth (seed was cracking). This shows that our isolate is probably not toxic to eukaryotic organisms.

experimental_design:
1. On a water agar plate, aliquot 10 uL each of the following: 
 a. Resuspended chemical extract 
 b. Methanol 
 c. Tetracycline 
 d. Amphotericin B 
 e. Deionized water 
 2. Leave one spot blank. 
 3. Place exactly 3 Salvia hispanica seeds in each aliquot; place 3 seeds in the empty spot as well. 
 4. Incubate at room temperature upright for 168 hours and monitor seed germination, stalk and root growth, and root hairiness.
results:
Spots containing chemical extract, deionized water, amphotericin B, and nothing exhibited normal germination, root & stalk length, and root hairiness. 
  
 Spots containing methanol and tetracycline exhibited shortened stalks. Methanol-grown seeds exhibited normal roots. Tetracycline-grown seed pods exhibited an unhealthy yellow color whereas all other pods were green.
